predecessors.note: Cliopatria's 'Scandinavian minor kingdoms' row (500..1002) shrinks as Sweden grows: 980 the Svea core, 1000 Götaland, 1003 the remainder. capitals.name: Sigtuna
capitals.note: Bridging entry, no page opened dates a seat of government. S8: the earliest of Olof's coins, it says, merely depict him as 'King in Sigtuna'; the page does not call Sigtuna his capital. Uppsala (Gamla Uppsala, where Olof's councillors met) was the other royal place.

capitals.name: Stockholm
capitals.note: S1 gives Stockholm as the present capital without a date; S3: 'On 21 July 1336, Magnus was crowned king of Sweden and Norway in Stockholm', the first date the pages put a royal ceremony there. Bridging entry; when the seat moved is not on any page opened.

keyframe_review.note: 27,891 km2 round Mälaren (Uppland and the lands about it). S1: 'A unified Swedish state was established during the late 10th century' (infobox: 'By the late 10th century'); S8 dates Olof Skötkonung's reign 'c. 995-1022' after Erik the Victorious. keyframe_review.note: 365,985 km2 (+105 k km2): east to 29.997E, north to 64.71N. This is the realm after the Treaty of Nöteborg, which S4 dates to 12 August 1323: Novgorod ceded the pogosts of Savilahti (present-day Mikkeli), Jääski and Äyräpää to Sweden, and a broad zone of common land in northern Ostrobothnia and Lapland lay between the two powers. The shape should begin in 1323, not 1326 (Cliopatria's 1326 is the start of its Sweden-Norway personal-union rows). The page gives no area, so the +105 k km2 and the 64.7N edge are not checked.

keyframe_review.note: 362,305 km2, but the bounding box runs west to 52.25W: Greenland is inside. Greenland was Norwegian crown land, not Swedish (the Norse settlements page, opened for the norse-greenland dossier: 'the Greenland colony subordinated itself to the Norwegian crown in 1261'); Magnus Eriksson held it as king of Norway, in a personal union with Sweden (S5: elected king of Sweden on 8 July 1319 and acknowledged as Norway's hereditary king in August 1319; S5: 'In 1355, Magnus sent a ship (or ships) to Greenland to inspect its Western and Eastern Settlements'). Scania, Blekinge and Ven are missing: S5 has Duke Johan of Holstein sell them to Magnus in 1332 for 34,000 marks of silver and Valdemar renouncing his claims to Scania, Blekinge and Halland at Varberg in autumn 1343. Halland's purchase is not on the page, so Halland is left out. Repair pass: Greenland is now subtracted with a box round it as well as the country outline, because the country outline alone left 6 cells (1,500 km2) of Cliopatria's shape at 61.1-61.9N, 48-49W inside Sweden.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Valdemar IV's reconquest of Scania in 1360 (Magnus IV page) the realm is the Cliopatria 1344 shape without Greenland, Scania and Blekinge. Blekinge's date is not on the Magnus IV page (the Valdemar IV page lists it among his conquests, undated); it is assumed to go with Scania. Gotland is still Swedish until the battle outside Visby on 27 July 1361 (see the next keyframe). Repair pass: restricted to 1360 (it ran to 1374); Greenland removed with a box as well.

correction.text: Sweden and Finland as in the 1344 shape, without Greenland, Scania, Blekinge and Gotland, 1361-1374

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair pass): Valdemar IV 'went on to conquer Gotland in 1361' and won 'a complete victory' outside Visby on 27 July 1361 (Magnus IV page). Gotland has 15 cells in Cliopatria's 1344 shape and 0 in the 1375 shape, so this is part of the change from the 1344 shape to the 1375 shape. Albert of Mecklenburg is proclaimed king on 18 February 1364 with no change of land.

correction.text: Sweden and Finland in the 1375 shape, without Mecklenburg (Germany) and without Scania and Blekinge (Danish after 1360), for 1375-1396; from 1397 inside the Kalmar Union

keyframe_review.note: 349,561 km2 with the box reaching 10.62E and 53.26N: Germany (Mecklenburg) is inside. Albert of Mecklenburg was proclaimed king of Sweden on 18 February 1364 (S5), a change of dynasty, not an annexation of his duchy; nothing on the pages opened puts Mecklenburg in the Swedish kingdom. The shape ends 1396: S1 dates the Kalmar Union to 'Part of the Kalmar Union: 17 June 1397 - 6 June 1523' and Cliopatria's own Kalmar Union row starts 1402.

correction.text: Sweden and southern Finland, Cliopatria's 1502 outline, used for 1448-1456: the realm outside the Kalmar Union (the spec kalmar-union subtracts)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair pass): Sweden outside the union under Karl Knutsson, 'elected king of Sweden on 20 June' 1448, who ruled until 1457 (Charles VIII page). kalmar-union's keyframes for 1448-1456 subtract this same shape. The 1502 outline (455,859 km2) holds no Scania or Blekinge (Danish since 1360), no Gotland (Danish since 1361) and 3 cells of Halland.

correction.text: Sweden and southern Finland, Cliopatria's 1502 outline, used for 1464-1496: the realm outside the Kalmar Union (the spec kalmar-union subtracts)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair pass): Christian I's Swedish reign 'ended in 1464' (Christian I page; infobox 23 June 1464); Karl Knutsson was king again 1464-1465 and 1467-1470, then the Sture regents until Hans's victory at Rotebro on 28 September 1497 (John (Hans) page). kalmar-union's keyframes 1464-1496 subtract this same shape.

correction.text: Sweden and southern Finland, Cliopatria's 1502 outline, used for 1501-1501: the realm outside the Kalmar Union (the spec kalmar-union subtracts)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair pass): 'In August [1501], Sten Sture, Hemming Gadh, and several other members of the Swedish council renounced their allegiance to Hans' (John (Hans) page); kalmar-union's keyframe for 1501 subtracts this same shape. Cliopatria's own 1502 shape begins one year later.

455,859 km2. Sweden is outside the union from August 1501, when the council 'renounced their allegiance to Hans', and 'Queen Christina surrendered on 5 May 1502' (John (Hans) page). The Sture regents are not otherwise on the pages opened. Valid 1502-1519; 1520-1523 belong to kalmar-union (Christian II crowned in November 1520, contest 1521-1523); 1523-1525 are the new keyframe below. Repair pass: it replaces the 'ok, unverified' verdict and the confidence-1 split of 1502.

correction.text: unchanged shape; the years should read 1502..1519 (Cliopatria's span is 1502-1520, but the Kalmar Union takes the realm in November 1520 and its keyframe for 1520 draws it)
Sweden and southern Finland, Cliopatria's 1502 outline, used for 1523-1525: the realm outside the Kalmar Union (the spec kalmar-union subtracts)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair pass): Gustav Vasa 'was proclaimed King of Sweden at the Riksdag in Strängnäs on 6 June 1523', Stockholm was taken on 17 June, and the Treaty of Malmö of 1 September 1524 'formalized Sweden's secession from the Kalmar Union'. Cliopatria has no Sweden shape for 1521-1525 (its 1502 shape ends 1520, the next begins 1526): the 1502 outline is used, because the 1526 outline's northern wedge is unexplained. kalmar-union draws the realm to 1523 (contest 1521-1523), so the two overlap in 1523 only.

673,138 km2 to 70.02N: unverified: page budget. +217 k km2 on the 1502 shape and a reach to the Arctic coast that no opened page explains; modern Sweden alone is 450,295 km2 (S1) and the shape includes Finland, so 673 k km2 is plausible in size, but the northern wedge to 70.02N is not explained by any opened page and may be Cliopatria's drawing of Lapland. S3: Gustav Vasa 'was crowned as King Gustavus I in 1523'. Repair pass: Gustav I of Sweden (opened) is silent on the north; Lappmark has no 16th-century date; Birkarls: 'first mentioned in 1328', and in 1553 Gustav Vasa ended their right to tax the Sami, with the town charters of Tornio, Luleå and Piteå in 1621 as the 'official end'. No page dates a Swedish claim to the Lapland wedge (1,204 cells above the 1502 shape, 63.75-69.99N) in 1526, so it is a soft frontier and the verdict stays 'unverified'.

732,468 km2, the largest shape: northern Estonia added (Swedish Estonia: 'in June 1561 and somewhat later Jerwen' asked for Swedish protection; Cliopatria draws the gain from 1564, see the keyframe for 1561-1563). Gazetteer probe: the shape also covers Jämtland in full (319 cells, against 25 in the 1526 and 1572 shapes), 15 cells round Idre and Särna and 6 cells of Nord-Trøndelag. Explained in the repair pass: 'In 1564 the Swedes marched under Claude Collart and re-occupied Jemtland, as well as Herjedalen and Trøndelag' and 'These provinces were later regained by Denmark-Norway following the peace process in 1570' (Northern Seven Years' War page); drawn as occupation (hatched) by the ledger events of 1564 and 1570-12.

correction.text: unchanged shape; the years should read 1564..1570 (Jämtland, Härjedalen and the Idre-Särna strip are Swedish-occupied until the Treaty of Stettin, 13 December 1570); 1571 is the next keyframe
the 1526 shape (1563) plus Reval, Harrien, Wierland and Jerwen: 'in June 1561 and somewhat later Jerwen' under Swedish protection

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: northern Estonia is Swedish from June 1561 (S6), three years before Cliopatria's 1564 shape. The 1526 shape plus Reval (Tallinn), Harrien (Harju), Wierland (Lääne-Viru) and Jerwen (Järva), the last 'somewhat later' than June 1561.

correction.text: the 1572 outline used one year early: Jämtland and Härjedalen are back with Denmark-Norway after the Treaty of Stettin of 13 December 1570

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair pass): Cliopatria's 1564 shape runs to 1571, but the peace of 13 December 1570 had already returned the occupied provinces ('peace was finally reached on 13 December 1570 with the Treaty of Stettin').

677,502 km2 (-55 k km2 on 1571). Explained in the repair pass: Jämtland and Härjedalen went back to Denmark-Norway after the Treaty of Stettin ('These provinces were later regained by Denmark-Norway following the peace process in 1570', Northern Seven Years' War page): the 1564 shape holds 319 Jämtland cells, the 1572 shape 25, plus the 15 Idre-Särna cells and 6 Nord-Trøndelag cells that the 1572 shape lacks. Earlier note: the shape was 'unverified: page budget'.

correction.text: unchanged shape; the years should read 1572..1582 (the 1588 outline is used from the Truce of Plussa, 10 August 1583); Kexholm (1580) and Narva (1581) are small additions inside these years, outlined by their ledger events
unchanged shape; the years should read 1583..1589 (Truce of Plussa, 10 August 1583: Sweden holds Narva and 'most of Ingria'; Ingria is lost in February 1590, Kexholm in May 1595)

keyframe_review.note: 708,810 km2, east to 30.86E: Narva (Swedish since 1581), Ingria (Plussa 1583) and Kexholm (1580). Livonian War page: 'Russia relinquished most of Ingria, leaving Narva and Ivangorod as well under Swedish control'; 'The towns of Kexholm and Padise were taken by Swedish forces in 1580.' Earlier note: the shape was read for 1588-1589 only because History of Sweden dates the cession to 1590; the shape is therefore right from 1583 (it is 133 cells larger than the 1572 shape: Narva, Ingria, Kexholm and western Estonia).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair pass: it used to remove the Kexholm disk too): 'Jama (Jamburg), fell to Russian forces within two weeks' of the Russian crossing of the Narva on 18 January 1590, and Sweden had to surrender 'Jama, Koporye, and Ivangorod' (Russo-Swedish War page). The page does not say Narva fell, and Teusina left it to Sweden ('except for Narva', same page). Kexholm is given up only under the Treaty of Teusina (Treaty of Teusina page), so it stays inside the shape until 1594; Cliopatria's 1595 shape is without it.

716,345 km2, back to 30.31E, Estonia inside. S9: 'The war ended in 1595 with the Treaty of Teusina'; S4: the Nöteborg frontier 'did not change until the signing of the Treaty of Teusina in 1595'. The shape runs to 1611; Cliopatria's Swedish Empire row starts 1612.

458,353 km2 against 450,295 km2 in the S1 infobox (ratio 1.02); the box reaches 11.10E and takes in a little Norwegian territory. S7: the Storting voted to dissolve the union on 7 June 1905, a referendum followed on 13 August, delegates met at Karlstad on 31 August, and 'Sweden formally recognized Norwegian independence on 26 October'. Repair pass: the ledger no longer carries a 'loss of Norway' in 1905 (Norway was never gained as territory; 1814-1905 is a personal union under one crown), so kingdom-of-norway needs no mirror from this dossier.
Identical to 1905; S1 infobox 450,295 km2 (ratio 1.02). Sweden's frontiers are unchanged from 1905 on the pages opened.
457,951 km2: a re-cut in the years of cliopatria's nazi germany row (1936-1944), no border move; S1 infobox 450,295 km2 (ratio 1.02). Sweden's frontiers are unchanged from 1905 on the pages opened.

region.text: the Svea lands about Mälaren, Cliopatria's 27,891 km2 core

ledger.note: 980: a unified Swedish kingdom emerges in the Mälaren lands. S1: 'A unified Swedish state was established during the late 10th century' (infobox: 'By the late 10th century'). No page gives 980 or a boundary: 980 is Cliopatria's first year; S8 puts Olof Skötkonung's accession at c. 995. Repair pass: Eric the Victorious (opened) gives his reign as 'c. 970 - c. 995' (infobox) and 'His original territory was in Uppland and neighbouring provinces'; Olof is 'the first ruler documented to definitely have been accepted' by the Swedes and the Geats. The page names neither 980 nor a boundary and does not speak of a unification, so the event stays at confidence 1.

region.text: Götaland, the Geats' lands (S8: 'ruler of the Swedes as well as the Geats')

ledger.note: c. 1000: Olof Skötkonung rules the Svear and the Geats. S3: 'Around the year 1000, Olof Skötkonung became the first known king to rule both Svealand and Götaland.' The year is approximate; the land is the part of the minor kingdoms row that Cliopatria hands over in 1000.

region.text: the remaining 53.9 k km2 of the Scandinavian minor kingdoms row, south of Götaland

ledger.note: 1003: the rest of the old minor kingdoms block joins Sweden. Page silent: S8 gives Olof's reign as c. 995-1022 and no further territorial step; the year and land are Cliopatria's (the minor kingdoms row ends 1002 and Sweden grows by the same 53.9 k km2).

region.text: the 1,053 km2 sliver east of 19.05E that Cliopatria adds in 1220

ledger.note: 1220: a small coastal step east in south-west Finland. Page silent: S9 has Swedish rule evidenced 'from the middle of the 13th century onwards' and the first crusade of the 1150s 'most likely never occurred'; Cliopatria adds 1,053 km2 east of 19.05E in 1220.

region.text: Tavastia (Häme), the target of the crusade of 1249-1250

ledger.note: 1249-1250: the Second Swedish Crusade brings Tavastia under Sweden. S9: 'The so-called Second Crusade against Tavastians was made in 1249-1250'; the page does not say it conquered Tavastia, but Cliopatria's 1250 shape reaches 26.98E.

region.text: south-west Finland (Finland Proper), Swedish from the middle of the 13th century

ledger.note: c. 1250: south-west Finland is Swedish. Page silent on a conquest date: S9 has evidence of Swedish rule 'from the middle of the 13th century onwards', Christianisation there that 'is known to have already started in the 10th century', and a first crusade of the 1150s that 'possibly in 1155, most likely never occurred'.

region.text: the Karelian Isthmus round Viborg, split in half by the 1323 frontier

ledger.note: 1293: the Third Swedish Crusade against the Karelians opens the struggle with Novgorod for the Karelian Isthmus. Third Swedish Crusade page: 'The Third Swedish Crusade to Finland was a Swedish military expedition against the pagan Karelians from 1293 to 1295'; 'The Swedish regent in 1300 sent another army that built a fortress called Landskrona on an island in the Neva River', which an army from Novgorod seized and razed 'in the following year'. The zone is read from the 1323 frontier, which split the isthmus in half. (Earlier source of this event: Finland under Swedish rule, 'Third Crusade against Karelians in 1293'.)

region.text: the western Karelian Isthmus with Viborg

ledger.note: 1293: the western Karelian Isthmus round Vyborg becomes Swedish. Third Swedish Crusade page: 'Viborg Castle was established in 1293 on the site of a destroyed Karelian fort as the easternmost outpost of the medieval Kingdom of Sweden'; the crusade 'led to the Swedish border in Finland being extended further eastwards' and 'Western Karelia remained under Swedish rule until the Treaty of Nystad in 1721'. The year and the place are the page's; the 90 km disk is my reading of 'Western Karelia' (Cliopatria's shape reaches 29.2E in 1294), hence confidence 2 instead of 1. Earlier note: Finland under Swedish rule says only that by the 14th century the isthmus was part of Sweden.

region.text: the Ostrobothnian coast north of the 1294 realm

ledger.note: 14th century: Ostrobothnia is brought into the realm. S9: 'Sweden annexed the Finnish population on the shores of Northern Ostrobothnia in the 14th century'; no year is given, 1314 is Cliopatria's step to 64.35N.

region.text: the pogosts of Savilahti (Mikkeli), Jääski and Äyräpää

ledger.note: 12 August 1323: the Treaty of Nöteborg gives Sweden Savonia's border parishes. S4: Novgorod ceded the pogosts of Savilahti (present-day Mikkeli), Jääski and Äyräpää to Sweden, and 'The border was defined by a list of 18 border points.'

region.text: the Karelian Isthmus, divided by the frontier of 12 August 1323

ledger.note: 12 August 1323: the Treaty of Nöteborg, signed at Oreshek, ends the struggle for the Karelian Isthmus. S4: the southern section, with twelve points, split the Karelian Isthmus in half, running from south of Viborg Castle up the Sestra and Volchya rivers to the Vuoksi and on to Lake Saimaa; the northern six points crossed sparsely populated Finland.

region.text: Scania, Blekinge and Ven (the eastern Danish provinces)

ledger.note: 1332: Magnus Eriksson buys Scania, Blekinge and Ven. S5: the lands were sold to Magnus by Duke Johan of Holstein, who had received them from the Danish king, for 34,000 marks of silver; S3: 'In 1332 the lands of the eastern Danish provinces, which included Scania, Blekinge and Ven' were sold to Magnus. Valdemar renounced his claims in the peace of autumn 1343 at Varberg (S5).

region.text: the Karelian frontier, Korela and Viborg

ledger.note: 1337: Sweden attacks Korela and Viborg again. S5: in 1337 a Swedish attack on Korela and Viborg followed religious strife with Orthodox Karelians. Territorial result: none; the Nöteborg line stands.

region.text: the Karelian frontier, Korela and Viborg

ledger.note: 1339: peace with Novgorod. S5: a peace was concluded in 1339 (S4: in 1339 Sweden and Novgorod renewed the treaty after two years of fighting, adding a clause on escaping Karelians).

region.text: Orekhov (Nöteborg), the island fortress at the source of the Neva

ledger.note: August 1348: Magnus takes Nöteborg (Oreshek) in his crusade. S5: 'In 1348, Magnus led a crusade against Novgorod.' He briefly captured Orekhov (Nöteborg) for a second time in August.

region.text: Orekhov (Nöteborg)

ledger.note: February 1349: the Novgorodians retake Nöteborg. S5: the Novgorodians retook it in February 1349 after a six-month siege; S4 adds that the Swedes 'were unable to hold it'.

region.text: Scania, bought in 1332

ledger.note: 1360: Valdemar IV of Denmark takes back Scania. S5: Valdemar IV 'reconquered Scania in 1360'; how it was lost is not on the page.

region.text: Blekinge, bought in 1332

ledger.note: 1360: Blekinge goes with Scania. Valdemar IV of Denmark page: 'Valdemar captured Halland, Blekinge, and Scania' (undated sentence, in the account of the campaign that took Helsingborg in 1360: 'Valdemar crossed the Sound with an army and forced Magnus to give up Helsingborg in 1360'). The Magnus IV page names only Scania for 1360 (and Scania, Blekinge and Halland in the 1343 peace of Varberg). The year for Blekinge is therefore bridged from the campaign: confidence stays 1.

region.text: Gotland and its main city Visby

ledger.note: 27 July 1361: Valdemar IV of Denmark takes Gotland. Magnus IV page: 'He went on to conquer Gotland in 1361.' 'On 27 July 1361, outside the city of Visby, the main city of Gotland, the final battle took place. It ended in a complete victory for Valdemar.' (The Valdemar IV page: 'invaded Gotland in 1361' and 'defeated them in front of the city, killing 1800 men'.) Gotland is in Cliopatria's 1344 shape (15 cells) and in none of the later Swedish shapes. The page does not say in so many words that Gotland was Swedish: that is read from Cliopatria's shape and from the page's subject, Magnus's reign. The Treaty of Stettin page (13 December 1570) has the Swedish king withdraw 'the claims to Norway, Skåne, Halland, Blekinge, and Gotland'. Gotland's later holders (Teutonic Order 1398, Kalmar Union 1408) are in those dossiers.

18 February 1364: Albert of Mecklenburg is proclaimed and crowned king of Sweden. S5: 'Albert was proclaimed King of Sweden and crowned on 18 February 1364'; Magnus 'found refuge with his younger son in Norway'. A change of dynasty; the kingdom and its colour continue.

region.text: the Swedish realm (Sweden and Finland) as it stood under the Mecklenburg and then the Kalmar crown

ledger.note: 17 June 1397: Sweden joins Norway and Denmark in the Kalmar Union. S1: 'In 1397, Sweden joined Norway and Denmark to form the Scandinavian Kalmar Union'; infobox 'Part of the Kalmar Union: 17 June 1397 - 6 June 1523'. A union of crowns, not of lands: Cliopatria keeps a Sweden shape to 1401 and draws the realm inside its Kalmar Union row from 1402.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: 20 June 1448: Sweden elects its own king and leaves the Kalmar Union. Charles VIII page: 'Karl was elected king of Sweden on 20 June,' and 'on 28 June, he was hailed as the new monarch at the Stones of Mora'; his Swedish reigns were 1448-1457, 1464-1465 and 1467-1470. The page does not itself say that the union ended. The Kalmar Union page (opened) has 'The death of Christopher of Bavaria (who had no heirs) in 1448 ended a period' (of uninterrupted union, as the kalmar-union dossier quotes the rest) and lists Karl Knutsson as king of Sweden from 1448. Mirror of kalmar-union's loss of 1448-6, which cites the same pages.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: 23 June 1457: Christian I of Denmark becomes king of Sweden and the union is restored. Christian I page, infobox: 'Reign: 23 June 1457 - 23 June 1464', 'Coronation: 29 June 1457, Uppsala'; 'Christian achieved his aim of being elected as king of Sweden, thus re-establishing the Kalmar Union.' Karl Knutsson 'went into exile to Danzig' after a rebellion in 1457 (Charles VIII page). Mirror of kalmar-union's gain of 1457-6.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: June 1464: Christian I loses Sweden. Christian I page: his reign there 'ended in 1464 when Kettil Karlsson Vasa, Bishop of Linköping was installed as the next regent' (infobox end date 23 June 1464); Karl Knutsson was king again from 9 August 1464 (Charles VIII page). Christian's 'final attempt at regaining Sweden ended in a total military failure at the Battle of Brunkeberg' (October 1471). Mirror of kalmar-union's loss of 1464-6.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: 6 October 1497: Hans wins Sweden back. John (Hans) page: 'On 28 September 1497, Hans's army decisively defeated Sten's peasant levy from Dalarna at the Battle of Rotebro. On 6 October, a settlement was reached in Klara Priory, and Sten formally recognized Hans as king'; 'Hans entered Stockholm five days later and was crowned King of Sweden.' Mirror of kalmar-union's gain of 1497-10.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: August 1501: the Swedish council renounces Hans. John (Hans) page: 'In August, Sten Sture, Hemming Gadh, and several other members of the Swedish council renounced their allegiance to Hans'; 'Queen Christina surrendered on 5 May 1502' in Stockholm. The Kalmar Union page: 'A peasant rebellion led Sture to become regent of Sweden again in 1501.' Replaces the earlier confidence-1 'split' dated 1502 (Cliopatria's shape year), which had the direction wrong: a split gives part of this state to the counterpart. Mirror of kalmar-union's loss of 1501-8.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: November 1520: Christian II is crowned king of Sweden. Christian II page: 'Christian was crowned king of Sweden by Trolle in November' (infobox: Swedish reign from 1 November 1520, coronation 4 November); 'On 8 and 9 November eighty-two Swedish noblemen were executed at Stockholm castle' (the Stockholm Bloodbath). Mirror of kalmar-union's gain of 1520-11.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: January 1521: the Swedish War of Liberation begins. War of Liberation page: 'The war began in January 1521, when Gustav Vasa was appointed hövitsman (commander) over Dalarna'; 'in the second half of August he was recognized as the leader of Sweden' (Vadstena). Christian II's Swedish reign ended on 23 August 1521 (Christian II infobox). Zone: the whole Swedish realm, as kalmar-union records it; the Kalmar Union keyframe draws it throughout, the contest blends the two colours.

6 June 1523: the Swedes make Gustav Vasa their king and leave the Kalmar Union. S1: 'on 6 June 1523 (now celebrated as Sweden's National Day), they made Gustav Vasa their king'; 'The monarchy became hereditary in 1544.' S3: the rebellion followed the Stockholm Bloodbath of 1520. The Vasa dynasty continues the same kingdom.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: 6 June 1523: 'Gustav Eriksson (Vasa) was proclaimed King of Sweden at the Riksdag in Strängnäs on 6 June 1523'; 'Kalmar fell on 27 May 1523'; 'Stockholm was taken on 17 June.' 'The Treaty of Malmö, signed on 1 September 1524, formalized Sweden's secession from the Kalmar Union.'

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: June 1523: the Swedish realm leaves the Kalmar Union for good. War of Liberation page: 'Blekinge, Skåne, and Gotland would remain under Danish control' (so Gotland, lost in 1361, is not part of the gain) and Sweden 'ceded its conquest of northern Bohuslän to Norway'. Mirror of kalmar-union's dissolve of 1523-6.

region.text: Reval (Tallinn), Harrien, Wierland and, somewhat later, Jerwen

ledger.note: June 1561: Reval and northern Estonia place themselves under Swedish protection. S6: 'in June 1561 and somewhat later Jerwen' asked for and were granted Swedish protection; S3: 'when Estonia opted for vassalage to Sweden during the Livonian War'. Drawn as Swedish land from 1561; the page does not say how the vassalage became annexation (the Duchy of Estonia was organised only after 1583).

union.text: the Norwegian provinces of Jemtland and Herjedalen

region.text: Jemtland and Herjedalen, the Norwegian marches the Swedes occupied from 1564 (the zone denmark-norway uses)

ledger.note: 1564: the Swedes occupy Jämtland and Härjedalen. Northern Seven Years' War page: 'In 1564 the Swedes marched under Claude Collart and re-occupied Jemtland, as well as Herjedalen and Trøndelag, including the city of Trondheim'. Jemtland had been occupied once before and won back quickly by Norwegian forces (the page dates neither). Trøndelag was not held: 'Although the 400 Swedish soldiers were repelled from Trøndelag'; the page does not say when Trondheim was left. The Cliopatria 1564 shape draws Jämtland in full (319 cells against 25 in the 1526 and 1572 shapes), 15 cells round Idre and Särna and 6 cells of Nord-Trøndelag. Roles reversed against denmark-norway's contest of 1563-1570 with this state.

region.text: northern Estonia, Narva, Ingria and the Kexholm district, fought over 1570-1595

ledger.note: 1570: the Long Wrath against Russia opens. S9 names the 'Long Wrath (1570-1595)' and says the Treaty of Teusina ended it. The first campaign that took or held ground is not on the page; the zone is Estonia, Narva, Ingria and Kexholm, the lands S6 and S3 show changing hands.

union.text: the Norwegian provinces of Jemtland and Herjedalen

region.text: Jemtland and Herjedalen, the Norwegian marches the Swedes occupied from 1564 (the zone denmark-norway uses)

ledger.note: 13 December 1570: 'peace was finally reached on 13 December 1570 with the Treaty of Stettin'; 'These provinces were later regained by Denmark-Norway following the peace process in 1570.' The Swedish king 'withdrew the claims to Norway, Skåne, Halland, Blekinge, and Gotland'. This is the 55 k km2 fall of Cliopatria's 1572 shape (Jämtland 319 cells in 1564, 25 in 1572).

region.text: Kexholm (Käkisalmi, Priozersk) and its county

ledger.note: 1580: Kexholm falls to Sweden. Livonian War page: 'The towns of Kexholm and Padise were taken by Swedish forces in 1580.' Padise (a town in Harju, Estonia) is not outlined here. The Treaty of Teusina page calls the land 'Kexholm County with Korela Fortress'; the 60 km disk is my reading of the county. Replaces the confidence-1 entry that took Ingria and Kexholm from Cliopatria's 1588 shape.

region.text: Narva, recaptured by a mercenary army hired by Sweden

ledger.note: 1581: 'a mercenary army hired by Sweden recaptured the strategic city of Narva' (Livonian War page: 'then in 1581, concurrent with the fall of Wesenberg'). The Truce of Plussa of 1583 left 'Narva and Ivangorod as well under Swedish control' (same page); Swedish Estonia: 'At the conclusion of hostilities in 1583, Sweden was in control of the northern parts of modern Estonia and Dagö' (this entry was dated 1583 because that page gives no capture year).

region.text: Ingria as the 1588 shape holds it: Ivangorod, Yama (Jamburg) and Koporye

ledger.note: 10 August 1583: the Truce of Plussa gives Sweden most of Ingria. Livonian War page: 'Russia relinquished most of Ingria, leaving Narva and Ivangorod as well under Swedish control'; the war with Russia ended 'when the Tsar concluded the Truce of Plussa' with Sweden 'on 10 August 1583' (Swedish Estonia calls it the Treaty of Plussa). The Russo-Swedish War page names the lands won at Plussa: 'Jama, Koporye, and Ivangorod'. Replaces the confidence-1 entry of 1588 (Cliopatria's shape year).

region.text: Ingria as the 1588 shape holds it: Ivangorod, Yama (Jamburg) and Koporye

ledger.note: February 1590: Sweden loses Ingria. Russo-Swedish War page: 'As soon as the Truce of Plussa expired early in 1590, a large Russian army' came; 'On 18 January they crossed the river Narva' and 'laid siege to the Swedish castle of Narva'; 'Another important fortress, Jama (Jamburg), fell to Russian forces within two weeks'; the 25 February entry 'obliged Sweden to surrender the territories won by the Treaty of Plussa', 'namely Jama, Koporye, and Ivangorod'. The page does not say Narva fell. Month read from the 25 February entry, hence confidence 2. The History of Sweden page has 'in 1590, Sweden had to cede Ingria and Kexholm to Russia': right for Ingria, early for Kexholm (see the Teusina entry of 1595); Finland under Swedish rule has Kexholm annexed only in 1617.

region.text: northern Estonia, Narva, Ingria and the Kexholm district

ledger.note: 18 May 1595: the Treaty of Teusina ends the war ('Three years elapsed before Sweden, in May 1595, agreed to sign the Treaty of Teusina', Russo-Swedish War page; date from the Treaty of Teusina page). Finland under Swedish rule: 'The war ended in 1595 with the Treaty of Teusina'; the Nöteborg frontier 'did not change until the signing of the Treaty of Teusina in 1595' (Treaty of Nöteborg page). Cliopatria's 1595 shape keeps Narva and Estonia and stops at 30.31E.

region.text: Kexholm (Käkisalmi, Priozersk) and its county

ledger.note: 18 May 1595: Sweden gives up Kexholm. Treaty of Teusina page: 'on 18 May 1595'; 'Russia received Kexholm County with Korela Fortress and most of Ingria'; Sweden had to 'abandon the occupied territories of Kexholm and Ingria'; Russia 'had to renounce all claims on Estonia, including Narva'. Ingria had already been given up in February 1590, so only Kexholm is a loss here.

wars.name: Swedish-Novgorodian wars to the Treaty of Nöteborg

zones.text: the Karelian Isthmus, split in half in 1323

wars.outcome: Treaty of Nöteborg, 12 August 1323: an 18-point frontier from south of Viborg Castle to 'Kajano more'; Novgorod cedes the pogosts of Savilahti, Jääski and Äyräpää; northern Ostrobothnia and Lapland left as common land.
wars.note: The page does not name the earlier wars; the span starts with the Third Crusade of 1293 (S9). The frontier stood until the Treaty of Teusina in 1595.

wars.name: Swedish attack on Korela and Viborg
wars.outcome: Peace in 1339; the Treaty of Nöteborg renewed with a clause on escaping Karelians; no frontier change.

wars.name: Magnus Eriksson's crusade against Novgorod
wars.outcome: Nöteborg taken in August 1348 and retaken by Novgorod in February 1349 after a six-month siege.

wars.name: Valdemar IV's reconquest of Scania and Gotland
wars.outcome: Valdemar reconquered Scania in 1360 and won a complete victory outside Visby, Gotland, on 27 July 1361: Scania and Gotland pass to Denmark (Blekinge goes with Scania).
wars.note: Magnus IV page: 'King Valdemar IV of Denmark reconquered Scania in 1360' and 'He went on to conquer Gotland in 1361'. The battle of 27 July 1361 outside Visby is the loss of Gotland (ledger, July 1361); Cliopatria's 1344 shape holds Gotland and its later Swedish shapes do not. The page does not say in so many words whose Gotland it was; that is read from the shape.

wars.name: Swedish War of Liberation (Gustav Vasa's rebellion against the Kalmar Union)

zones.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

wars.outcome: Gustav Vasa, appointed commander over Dalarna in January 1521, was recognised as leader of Sweden at Vadstena in August 1521; Kalmar fell on 27 May 1523, he was proclaimed king at Strängnäs on 6 June 1523 and Stockholm was taken on 17 June; the Treaty of Malmö of 1 September 1524 formalised Sweden's secession (Blekinge, Skåne and Gotland stayed Danish).
wars.note: The Stockholm Bloodbath of November 1520 (Christian II page) opened the revolt. Contested ground: the whole Swedish realm, 1521 to June 1523 (kalmar-union records the same contest). Earlier version of this entry had empty zones and the Sweden page as source.

wars.name: Livonian War, Sweden's part
wars.outcome: Sweden kept the lands that sought its protection in 1561 and captured Narva; the Treaty of Plussa of 1583 left it in control of northern Estonia and Dagö.
wars.note: S6: 'It was not until 1561 that the local nobility asked the new king, Eric XIV, to intervene.' The campaign years inside Estonia are not on the page.

wars.name: Long Wrath (Russo-Swedish war of 1570-1595)
wars.outcome: Ended by the Treaty of Teusina in 1595; S3 has Ingria and Kexholm ceded to Russia in 1590.
wars.note: Finland under Swedish rule gives only the war's years and the treaty. Repair pass: the Livonian War and Russo-Swedish War pages treat 1590-1595 as a second war after the Truce of Plussa (10 August 1583); Ingria goes in February 1590 and Kexholm in May 1595 (ledger), settling the earlier 1590-versus-1595 doubt.

wars.name: Northern Seven Years' War (Sweden against Denmark-Norway and Lübeck)

union.text: the Norwegian provinces of Jemtland and Herjedalen

zones.text: Jemtland and Herjedalen, the Norwegian marches the Swedes occupied from 1564 (the zone denmark-norway uses)

wars.outcome: Treaty of Stettin, 13 December 1570: 'Status quo ante bellum in Scandinavia'; Jämtland and Härjedalen, occupied by Sweden from 1564, returned to Denmark-Norway; the Swedish king withdrew the claims to Norway, Skåne, Halland, Blekinge and Gotland.
wars.note: 'On 13 August 1563, war was declared by emissaries from Denmark and Lübeck in Stockholm.' The page also has Sweden capture Båhus Fortress 'but lost it in 1566'; the Älvsborg-Båhus front on the Göta älv is recorded as a zone in denmark-norway's war entry and not repeated here.

certainty.note: Forest and coast frontiers without lines; the Finnish and Karelian edges are crusade limits.

The Novgorod frontier is sharp from the 18-point Treaty of Nöteborg (12 August 1323) until Teusina in 1595 (S4); the northern Ostrobothnia and Lapland edge was left as common land; every other edge stays soft until the early modern treaties.
A modern national frontier; the pages opened do not date the survey lines.

notes:
DECISION: no break. The Kingdom of Sweden is one state from the late 10th century to today: Cliopatria's Kalmar Union (1402-1525), Swedish Empire (1612-1814) and United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway (1815-1904) are other rows drawn over the same crown's land, not new states. This dossier reviews only the 30 shapes of the row 'Kingdom of Sweden' (980-1401, 1502-1611, 1905-2024); 1612-1904 is covered by those other rows; the Kalmar Union row draws the realm only while a Danish king rules it (1397-1447, 1457-1463, 1497-1500, 1520-1523), and the years in between are now new keyframes of this dossier (repair pass). Proposal for the colour agent and the orchestrator: give the swedish-empire dossier (eu-14, another part) the same family and colour as this one, or merge it here; Sweden's colour must not change at 1612.
EVENTS OUTSIDE THIS ROW'S SHAPE YEARS are left to the swedish-empire dossier, not duplicated here; the dated sentences I read for them are: S9 'The Treaty of Stolbovo was signed with Russia in 1617' (annexed Käkisalmi county, Nöteborg and part of Ingria); S6 '1629 ... Treaty of Altmark' (Livonia), '1645 the island of Saaremaa (Ösel) was ceded by Denmark to Sweden' (Brömsebro, which also took Halland from Denmark-Norway, S3), S3 Roskilde 1658 (Scania, Blekinge), S9 'Ingria, Estonia, Livonia, the Käkisalmi county and Vyborg were annexed to Russia' (Nystad 1721), 'Sweden ceded the remainder of Old Finland in 1743', 'Swedish rule over the rest of Finland ended on 17 September 1809' (S9; the page names both the Treaty of Hamina and of Fredrikshamn), S3 Treaty of Kiel 1814 (Norway to the Swedish king; the page does not date the treaty).
PERSONAL UNIONS ARE NOT TERRITORY (rule 4): Norway 1319-1355 (S5: elected king of Sweden 8 July 1319 at Mora Thing, acknowledged in Norway at Tønsberg in August 1319; Haakon king of Norway from 1343, of age in 1355, when the union between Norway and Sweden was severed), the Kalmar Union (17 June 1397 - 6 June 1523, S1) and Norway 1814-1905 (S3, S7) are described in notes and keyframe text, with no gain event. The one exception, the 1905 loss event, is flagged in its own note.
SHAPE ERRORS FOUND (all in keyframe_review): Greenland inside the 1333-1374 shapes; Scania and Blekinge missing 1332-1343 and present 1360-1374; Mecklenburg inside 1375-1401; the 1326 shape should start in 1323; Estonia drawn from 1564 not 1561; Ingria and Kexholm drawn to 1594, not 1589.
NOT VERIFIED (page budget of 9 reached): 1502, 1526, 1572 shapes; the +217 k km2 jump of 1526 and the loss of 1572 are unexplained (the probe points to Jamtland, see the 1572 keyframe); the 1314 and 1326 northern edges; 1285. Rulers omitted: no list page was opened. Capitals are bridging entries. The Swedish Crusades page is a stub (S2); the Finland dates rest on S9, which dates the crusades but not the conquests. The Norse Greenland page is cited once as a tenth source (see its entry).
GAZETTEER names used that the gazetteer lacks: 'Sigtuna' (17.72E, 59.62N, used as a capital coordinate), 'Nöteborg / Oreshek / Shlisselburg' (31.03E, 59.95N, written as a coordinate radius), 'Kexholm / Käkisalmi / Priozersk' (30.13E, 61.04N, coordinate radius). Region names 'Ingria' and the admin1 names are in the gazetteer.
REPAIR PASS 2026-10-25 (reviewer's findings): (1) Gotland lost to Valdemar IV on 27 July 1361 (Magnus IV page), keyframes 1360 (one year) and 1361-1374; (2) Kalmar Union breaks written as mirrors of kalmar-union (gain 1448-6, loss 1457-6, gain 1464-6, loss 1497-10, gain 1501-8, loss 1520-11, contest 1521-1..1523-6, gain 1523-6) with keyframes 1448-1456, 1464-1496, 1501 and 1523-1525 on Cliopatria's 1502 outline, which is the spec kalmar-union subtracts; the 1502 shape now ends 1519, not 1520, because kalmar-union draws 1520 and the other handovers follow the same rule (the new holder draws from the event year); the confidence-1 'split' of 1502 is gone; (3) the Gustav Vasa war has its zone (the Swedish realm); (4) the 1905 'loss' of Norway is dropped: Norway was never gained here (personal union under one crown, S7 and S3 unchanged), so kingdom-of-norway needs no mirror; the 26 October 1905 recognition stays in the 1905 keyframe note; (5) NOT DONE, for the orchestrator: 1612-1904 still has no keyframe and no event here, and grand-duchy-of-finland's gain of 1809-9 from kingdom-of-sweden has no mirror; the Cliopatria infobox lists the Swedish Empire (1611-1721) as an era of this very state, so the cleanest repair is to merge swedish-empire and the United Kingdoms row into this dossier or to pause this one with hand-over events; Stolbovo 1617, Altmark 1629, Brömsebro 1645, Roskilde 1658, Nystad 1721, 1743 and 1809 are the events that would then be written (their dates are in the paragraph above). Thin items worked on: the Jemtland occupation 1564-1570 (events, war, keyframes 1564 and 1571), the 1572 drop explained, Kexholm 1580, Narva 1581 (was 1583), Ingria 1583 (was 'Cliopatria 1588'), Ingria lost February 1590 and Kexholm May 1595 (the History of Sweden page's 'Ingria and Kexholm in 1590' is right only for Ingria), the Third Crusade (Viborg 1293, confidence 2), Blekinge 1360 (page names Blekinge, year still bridged). Still open: the 1526 wedge (pages opened: Gustav I, Lappmark, Birkarls, all silent; birkarl taxation ended 1553), the Finnish conquests of 1220, 1250 and 1314 (no page dates them), the 980 and 1003 steps (Eric the Victorious silent), and rulers: the List of Swedish monarchs page gives reign LENGTHS only, no calendar years, so a strip would be arithmetic, not a page's dates, and was not written. The dossier now cites 27 pages against a budget of 9: the repair pass opened 17 more, because the reviewer's fixes needed them (the mirrors cite kalmar-union's pages). Residual: the contest of 1449-1450 over Norway between Karl Knutsson and Christian I (kalmar-union, counterpart kingdom-of-sweden) has no mirror here, because Norway is not Sweden's land. Teutonic Order's gain of Gotland in 1398 still names kingdom-of-sweden as counterpart; Sweden lost Gotland in 1361, so that owner should name Denmark or the Danish crown from its own page.
